title: Private Tutor Tax Returns: Fees, Platforms and Term-Time Records
excerpt: Tutoring income can come from direct lessons, agencies and online platforms. Before preparing a return, establish whether each arrangement is employment or self-employment and keep the evidence supporting that treatment.
metaTitle: Private Tutor Tax Returns: Fees and Record Checklist | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare tutor tax records across private lessons, agencies and platforms. Reconcile fees and refunds, separate PAYE work and check the tax-year cut-off.
featuredImageAlt: A private tutor reconciles term-time lesson diary, platform payouts and direct-client fees at a desk.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Working for yourself
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Overview
GOV.UK — Check if you need to tell HMRC about your income from online platforms

content:
Tutoring income can come from direct lessons, agencies and online platforms. Before preparing a return, establish whether each arrangement is employment or self-employment and keep the evidence supporting that treatment.

Separate school employment from private work

A tutor may be paid through PAYE by a school and receive separate private lesson fees. The employment income belongs with the employment records; genuine self-employed activity needs its own business calculation.

An agency calling you self-employed does not, by itself, settle employment status. Keep the contract and explain who sets the work, controls the arrangement and pays you if the position is uncertain.

Record the full lesson income

Keep a schedule of fees, cancellations, refunds and amounts received through platforms. Platform charges may be deducted before payout, so retain statements showing the underlying lesson income and fees.

If a parent pays for a block of lessons, note what the payment covers and any refund conditions. The accounting method affects timing; do not move receipts between tax years simply to match school terms.

Review business costs carefully

Relevant teaching materials, platform charges, insurance and a reasonable business portion of certain running costs may be deductible where the rules are met. Private costs and mixed-use equipment need review rather than a blanket percentage copied from another tutor.

Travel also needs checking. A journey related to tutoring is not automatically deductible under every working arrangement, and the rules differ from an employee expense claim.

Prepare for the correct tax year

For a 2025/26 online return, gather records covering 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026; the usual filing deadline is 31 January 2027. Summer holidays and the academic year do not change those tax-year boundaries.

Tell TaxSimba about employment, private pupils, agency contracts and platform income. The accountant can then confirm the scope and review the information needed for your return. If gross self-employment income grows, check MTD separately instead of waiting until the next annual filing season to consider it.

Put it into practice

A block booking needs a clear payment trail

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A tutor receives £400 for a block of lessons and later refunds £80 after a cancellation. She keeps the booking agreement, receipt date and refund record, then explains the accounting basis used. She does not record the original payment again each time a lesson is delivered. Her school PAYE job is kept in the employment pack, and platform fees are reconciled separately. The academic term does not replace the UK tax-year boundary.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Employment or self-employed tutoring?Provide contracts and actual working arrangements for each source.
How do fees, blocks and refunds reconcile?Keep the booking and payment trail without duplicating each delivered lesson.
Do exports match the tax year?Check dates and accounting method rather than using a school-year total.

Two more questions you may have

Can I report only the platform payout?

Keep the gross lesson and fee breakdown so income and expenses can be reconciled correctly.

Does an agency's self-employed label settle my status?

No. The real working arrangements matter. Provide the contract and relevant facts.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • List PAYE, private, agency and platform work.
  • Record lesson fees, block payments and refunds.
  • Reconcile platform fees and payouts.
  • Collect teaching-material and other business-cost evidence.
  • Check tax-year coverage and accounting method.

title: Personal Trainer Tax: Gym Fees, Client Packages and Online Coaching
excerpt: A personal trainer can be employed by a gym, self-employed, or have a mixture of arrangements. Your tax records should reflect the actual contracts and income sources rather than assuming every fitness payment is treated alike.
metaTitle: Personal Trainer Tax: Clients, Gym Fees and Packages | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare personal trainer tax records for gym work, client packages and online coaching, with clear refunds, fees, employment and business-cost evidence.
featuredImageAlt: A personal trainer reconciles prepaid client sessions, gym rent and online coaching statements, modest weights nearby.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Working for yourself
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Overview
GOV.UK — Check if you need to tell HMRC about your income from online platforms

content:
A personal trainer can be employed by a gym, self-employed, or have a mixture of arrangements. Your tax records should reflect the actual contracts and income sources rather than assuming every fitness payment is treated alike.

Identify who pays you and why

Keep gym contracts, client invoices and online coaching statements. Separate wages taxed through PAYE from genuine self-employed session fees. Where a gym collects payments and retains an amount, establish whether it is paying wages or settling your business receipts after charges.

The contract wording alone may not settle employment status. Explain the practical arrangement if control, substitution or financial risk makes the position uncertain.

Track packages and refunds

A client may buy several sessions in advance, cancel or receive a refund. Keep records of the amount received, what was promised and any money returned. Your accounting method determines the relevant timing for the tax calculation.

For example, a bank deposit for ten sessions should be traceable to that client's agreement. It should not be entered again as new income every time a session is delivered without checking how the initial payment was recorded.

Business spending needs a business purpose

Gym rental, relevant insurance, booking charges and qualifying equipment may be allowable where the conditions are met. Ordinary sports clothing, personal gym use and personal food are not automatically deductible because you work in fitness.

Training costs require particular care. Updating skills used in an existing business and obtaining skills for a new activity can have different tax treatment. Keep the course details and explain their connection to the work.

Give the accountant a complete picture

Supply platform statements, cash income records, contracts, receipts and employment information. If clients pay from abroad, tell the accountant rather than assuming the platform has dealt with all tax consequences.

TaxSimba can confirm the appropriate personal tax service and required records. If you also sell products, run separate activities or approach MTD thresholds, raise those facts before the return is prepared so the scope matches how the business actually operates.

Put it into practice

A prepaid package is not fresh income every session

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A trainer receives £600 for a package of sessions. She records the agreement and payment once, tracks delivery and any refund, and tells the accountant the accounting method used. Where a gym retains fees before paying her, she supplies the underlying statement. She keeps PAYE employment separate and identifies private gym use, food and ordinary sportswear rather than treating everything fitness-related as a business cost. Training-course details are provided for their own tax review.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Who pays you under which arrangement?Separate gym employment, direct clients and genuine self-employed contracts.
Can packages and refunds be traced?Connect payments to agreements without double-counting sessions.
Is spending genuinely for the existing business?Explain course content, equipment use and private elements before claiming.

Two more questions you may have

Are sports clothes automatically deductible for a trainer?

No. Ordinary clothing is not automatically allowable because it is worn for work. Give the accountant item details.

Can every fitness qualification be claimed?

Not automatically. The skills, business connection and current rules need checking; keep the course information.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect gym contracts and PAYE documents.
  • List client packages and payment dates.
  • Record refunds and platform deductions.
  • Gather relevant rental, insurance and equipment evidence.
  • Explain courses and private-use costs.

title: Self-Employed Cleaner Tax Returns: Cash Payments and Business Records
excerpt: Cash paid by customers is still business income. A self-employed cleaner needs records of cash and bank payments, along with evidence of genuine business costs, to prepare an accurate tax return.
metaTitle: Self-Employed Cleaner Tax: Cash and Business Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Keep cleaner tax records complete across cash, bank and agency payments. Separate employment, business supplies, private use and supported travel costs.
featuredImageAlt: A self-employed cleaner records both cash and bank customer payments, cleaning caddy beside organised books.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Working for yourself
GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: Overview
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Overview

content:
Cash paid by customers is still business income. A self-employed cleaner needs records of cash and bank payments, along with evidence of genuine business costs, to prepare an accurate tax return.

Check the working arrangement first

You may clean directly for customers, work through an agency or be employed. Establish which arrangement applies to each source of work. Agency involvement does not automatically make a person self-employed, and PAYE wages should not be mixed into sole trader sales.

Keep contracts, payment statements and any employment documents. If the status is unclear, explain who sets the hours, supplies equipment, controls the work and carries the financial risk.

Keep a simple income trail

Use a diary or booking system to record jobs, amounts charged, refunds and payment method. Reconcile cash received to deposits and business spending. Paying cash directly for supplies does not remove the need to record the original customer receipt.

For example, if a customer pays £80 and you use £15 of it for supplies, the records should explain £80 income and the separate £15 cost. Recording only the £65 later banked hides part of the activity.

Distinguish business and private costs

Qualifying cleaning materials, equipment, insurance and business charges may be deductible. Where supplies or equipment are also used at home, identify the business portion. Normal clothing and personal household costs are not automatically allowable.

Travel between jobs may require a different analysis from journeys to a regular workplace. Keep dates, destinations and reasons rather than assuming every mile qualifies.

Prepare early if records are incomplete

Ask agencies for missing statements and use your booking history to identify gaps. Reconstructed figures should have a reasonable evidence trail; they should not be invented to produce a preferred tax result.

TaxSimba can review the information needed for your agreed return or MTD service. Tell the accountant about every payment route and any employment as well as direct customers. Regular records make it easier to answer questions while the jobs and payments are still familiar.

Put it into practice

Cash spent before banking is still part of the records

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A cleaner receives £100 cash from a customer, buys £18 business supplies and banks £82. She records £100 income and the separate £18 cost, with the receipt. Recording only the banked amount would conceal both parts. She also keeps agency statements and employment documents distinct. A booking diary helps identify missing payments, while journey records explain work travel rather than assuming all home-to-job mileage qualifies.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Are all customer payment methods recorded?Reconcile cash received, cash spent and bank deposits without omitting income.
Is agency work employment or self-employment?Provide the actual arrangement and relevant statements.
Are costs partly private?Identify household supplies, equipment and journey use before calculating a claim.

Two more questions you may have

Is cash income irrelevant if I never bank it?

No. Record the customer receipt and any separate business spending from that cash.

Can my booking diary replace every document?

It helps explain activity, but keep invoices, statements and expense evidence as well.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Maintain a job and payment-method diary.
  • Reconcile cash received, spent and banked.
  • Collect agency and employment records.
  • Retain supply and equipment receipts.
  • Log business travel and private-use information.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Rent a Room Relief: When Lodger Income Needs a Tax Return
excerpt: Rent a Room relief can apply to furnished accommodation in your only or main home. It is different from the rules for an ordinary buy-to-let property, and the gross receipts matter when checking the threshold.
metaTitle: Rent a Room Relief: Lodger Receipts and Tax Returns | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check Rent a Room conditions, gross receipts and shared-income limits, then compare the scheme with normal expenses where a return is needed.
featuredImageAlt: A homeowner discusses lodger receipts and letting period with adviser, welcoming spare-room doorway background.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Rent a room in your home: The Rent a Room Scheme
GOV.UK — PIM4001 - Rent-a-room: overview - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance

content:
Rent a Room relief can apply to furnished accommodation in your only or main home. It is different from the rules for an ordinary buy-to-let property, and the gross receipts matter when checking the threshold.

The basic threshold

The scheme allows qualifying receipts of up to £7,500 a year tax-free. The limit is halved to £3,750 if someone else receives income from letting accommodation in the same residence. Do not assume each person gets a full £7,500 simply because they have separate bank accounts.

Check all relevant receipts, including amounts for associated services. The test is not just the profit left after household costs. The accommodation and living arrangements must also satisfy the scheme's conditions.

What if receipts exceed the limit?

You need to compare the available tax treatments rather than automatically deducting the allowance and also claiming ordinary expenses. The scheme and normal profit calculation are alternatives under the relevant rules; the same costs should not receive double relief.

For example, a live-in landlord with receipts above the threshold should give the accountant both the full receipts and expenses. That allows the correct comparison and any required election to be considered.

A lodger is not every type of tenant

Letting a separate property, letting business premises or living abroad can raise different conditions. Tell your accountant what accommodation is let, whether it is furnished and when you lived there. A website describing the arrangement as a room rental does not establish eligibility.

MTD can require additional records

People already in MTD should not assume Rent a Room income can always be left outside digital records. HMRC has particular rules where other property income or receipts above the scheme threshold are involved. The relief and the record-keeping question need checking separately.

TaxSimba can confirm the information needed for the personal tax service. Supply ownership details, receipts, service charges and any other rental income so the accountant can assess the actual arrangement rather than apply the allowance in isolation.

Put it into practice

Services and shared receipts affect the check

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A live-in landlord receives room rent plus amounts for associated services. She totals the relevant gross receipts rather than using the amount left after household costs. She explains whether someone else also receives income from the same residence and supplies occupancy dates and accommodation details. If receipts exceed the applicable threshold, the accountant compares the permitted scheme treatment with normal income-and-expense treatment. She does not deduct the allowance and the same ordinary costs together.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Does the accommodation meet the conditions?Describe the furnished space, main-home use and occupancy dates.
What are the relevant gross receipts?Include associated services and identify any shared income.
Which treatment is appropriate above the limit?Compare the permitted alternatives and any required election using full records.

Two more questions you may have

Does each person always get a full £7,500 threshold?

No. The limit is halved where the relevant income is shared. Check the actual arrangement.

Is an ordinary buy-to-let automatically covered?

No. Rent a Room concerns qualifying accommodation in your home, with specific conditions.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Describe the accommodation and when you lived there.
  • Total relevant rent and service receipts.
  • Identify anyone sharing the income.
  • Keep actual expense evidence for comparison.
  • Check the applicable threshold, reporting and election position.

title: Landlord Furniture and Appliances: Replacement of Domestic Items Relief
excerpt: Replacing a tenant's worn-out appliance may qualify for a different tax treatment from buying furniture for a property for the first time. Check the replacement rules before claiming every furnishing purchase as a rental expense.
metaTitle: Landlord Furniture and Appliances: Replacement Relief | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check replacement of domestic items relief, distinguish initial furnishing and fixtures, and keep evidence of the old item, equivalent replacement and disposal.
featuredImageAlt: A landlord compares an old worn appliance with replacement invoice and a similar replacement appliance.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property
GOV.UK — PIM3210 - Furnished lettings: Replacement of domestic items relief: 2016-17 onwards - HMRC internal manual

content:
Replacing a tenant's worn-out appliance may qualify for a different tax treatment from buying furniture for a property for the first time. Check the replacement rules before claiming every furnishing purchase as a rental expense.

What the relief is intended to cover

Replacement of domestic items relief can apply to qualifying replacements of items such as furniture, household appliances, furnishings and kitchenware used in a residential letting. The old item must have been provided for the tenant's use and replaced under the relevant conditions.

The cost of initially furnishing a property does not qualify under this replacement relief. Fixtures and work to the building can also fall under different rules, so a fitted installation should not automatically be treated like a freestanding appliance.

Improvements can restrict the claim

Where the replacement is an improvement, the allowable amount may be limited to the cost of a suitable equivalent replacement. Incidental costs and any proceeds from disposing of the old item also need considering.

For example, replacing an ordinary fridge with a substantially more expensive upgraded model does not necessarily make the whole price deductible under the relief. Give the accountant information about both the old item and the new purchase.

Keep evidence of what was replaced

Retain the purchase invoice, delivery or disposal costs and any amount received for the old item. Note the property, when the original item was supplied and why it needed replacing. A brief record at the time is easier than reconstructing the history several years later.

Mixed personal use, connected arrangements and particular relief regimes can affect eligibility. Rent a Room treatment should also be checked before assuming replacement relief is available alongside it.

Avoid counting the cost twice

If the letting agent paid for the replacement and deducted it from rent, provide the statement and underlying invoice. Reconcile that deduction to the bank payout so the same purchase is not claimed again separately.

TaxSimba can review the evidence within the agreed rental tax service. Describe the replacement clearly and let the accountant distinguish domestic items, building repairs and improvements before finalising the return.

Put it into practice

An upgrade needs an equivalent-cost comparison

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A landlord replaces a worn freestanding fridge with a substantially upgraded model. She keeps the invoice, details of the old fridge, a suitable equivalent's cost, delivery and disposal charges, and any sale proceeds for the old item. The accountant checks the qualifying replacement amount rather than assuming the full upgraded price is deductible. The agent's statement is reconciled too, so a purchase paid from retained rent is not claimed again as a separate bank expense.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Replacement or first furnishing?Document the old tenant-use item and what replaced it.
Is the new item an improvement?Keep equivalent-replacement information so any restriction can be checked.
What incidental costs and proceeds exist?Record delivery, disposal and sale proceeds and avoid duplicating agent-paid costs.

Two more questions you may have

Does initially furnishing a rental qualify under replacement relief?

No. This relief concerns qualifying replacements, not simply every furniture purchase.

Are building fixtures treated like freestanding appliances?

Not automatically. Describe the item and installation so the correct repairs, capital or domestic-item rules can be checked.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Identify the property and old item.
  • Keep the replacement invoice and date.
  • Record equivalent-cost evidence for an upgrade.
  • List delivery, disposal and old-item proceeds.
  • Reconcile any agent payment to avoid double claims.

sources.label: GOV.UK — PIM2510 - Beginning and end of a property business: cessation - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property

content:
A gap between tenants does not automatically end a rental business. Some costs during a genuine void period may remain allowable, but the purpose of the spending and what happens to the property matter.

Establish whether the letting business continues

Keep evidence that the property remains available for letting, such as agent correspondence, advertising and plans to obtain another tenant. A temporary vacancy differs from moving into the property yourself or withdrawing it permanently from rental use.

If the property is being sold or converted to personal use, tell your accountant when the decision was made and how the property was used. There is no universal rule that every cost remains deductible until the eventual sale date.

Review costs individually

Insurance, utilities, council tax, advertising and repairs can need considering during a continuing letting business. Each cost must still satisfy the normal rules. Capital improvements and private expenditure do not become deductible simply because no rent was received that month.

For example, replacing a broken component between tenants can differ from extending the property or carrying out substantial improvements. Supply invoices describing the work rather than a single bank entry labelled refurbishment.

First letting and later vacancies differ

Costs before the rental business starts have their own rules. A newly purchased property undergoing work before its first tenant should not automatically be treated in the same way as an established rental property briefly awaiting a replacement tenant.

If you own several rental properties, explain which remain let and which are empty. The overall UK property business and the facts of the individual expense both need considering.

Keep the chronology with the documents

Record the last tenant's leaving date, marketing dates, personal occupation if any and the next tenancy start date. Link each expense to that timeline and retain proof of payment.

TaxSimba can use those facts to review the rental calculation within your agreed service. If a long void creates a loss or the business may have ceased, raise that separately so the accountant can check the correct treatment rather than carry the same assumptions into another tax year.

Put it into practice

Keep the timeline beside the invoices

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A tenant leaves in June and the next tenant arrives in September. The landlord retains marketing instructions, adverts and tenancy dates, linking insurance and repair invoices to that continuing letting period. If she instead decides to occupy the property personally or withdraw it permanently, she records the decision and use dates. Those facts matter: neither an empty property nor the absence of rent makes every cost deductible, and capital improvements remain a separate question.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Is the letting business continuing?Keep marketing and agent evidence of an intention to relet.
Did the use or intention change?Record personal occupation, withdrawal or sale plans with dates.
What did each expense achieve?Distinguish normal running costs, repairs, capital work and private spending.

Two more questions you may have

Are first-tenant setup costs the same as a later vacancy?

Not necessarily. Pre-commencement costs have their own rules. Provide purchase and first-letting history.

Can I deduct every cost until a sale completes?

No universal rule says that. The continuing-business position, purpose and nature of each cost need checking.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Record the last tenancy end date.
  • Retain re-letting instructions and advertisements.
  • Document any personal use or changed plans.
  • Link expenses to the vacancy timeline.
  • Record the next tenancy or permanent cessation details.

title: Living Abroad With UK Rental Income: Withholding and Your Tax Return
excerpt: Living outside the UK does not automatically make UK rental income tax-free. The Non-resident Landlords Scheme can affect how rent is paid, while the annual tax return establishes the wider liability.
metaTitle: Non-Resident Landlord: Withholding and UK Tax Returns | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Separate Non-resident Landlords Scheme withholding from final UK tax. Prepare gross rent, certificates, residence facts and any gross-payment approval.
featuredImageAlt: A landlord abroad reviews UK letting statements and withholding certificates on a video call with UK accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax on your UK income if you live abroad: Rental income
GOV.UK — What the Non-resident Landlords Scheme is

content:
Living outside the UK does not automatically make UK rental income tax-free. The Non-resident Landlords Scheme can affect how rent is paid, while the annual tax return establishes the wider liability.

The scheme and tax residence are different tests

HMRC's guidance treats a landlord living abroad for six months or more a year as a non-resident landlord for the scheme, even where the person is UK resident for tax purposes. Your residence status needs its own assessment; do not infer it solely from a flight itinerary or overseas address.

Supply travel dates, living arrangements and other relevant facts if residence needs reviewing. Double tax agreements and entitlement to allowances can also matter.

Tax may be withheld before you receive rent

Letting agents, and in some cases tenants, must operate the scheme unless HMRC has authorised payment without deduction. Ask for statements and tax certificates showing rent, deductible costs used in the withholding calculation and tax paid over.

For example, an agent's net transfer can already reflect management charges and withheld tax. Recording only that deposit as rent can lose both the gross income and a credit for tax already deducted.

Gross-payment approval is not an exemption

Permission to receive rental income without deduction does not mean there is no UK tax to pay. The annual reporting and payment position still needs checking. The scheme's quarterly withholding calculation is not necessarily the final calculation of your rental profit or liability.

Confirm the filing route and service scope

Non-residence can require supplementary information and suitable filing software. If you are also within MTD, the software and agent arrangements must support the actual circumstances; do not assume an ordinary resident-landlord process is sufficient.

Ask TaxSimba to confirm acceptance and scope before purchasing support for a non-resident case. Provide ownership details, rental statements, withholding certificates and relevant foreign tax information. A clear review at the start helps distinguish the UK rental return from any residence, treaty or overseas filing advice needing separate specialist work.

Put it into practice

The net transfer can hide a tax credit

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

An overseas landlord's agent statement includes gross rent, fees and tax withheld under the scheme. She provides the full statement and certificate rather than entering the net bank transfer as rent. Approval to receive rent without deduction would change withholding, not necessarily eliminate UK tax or filing. She also supplies residence history and foreign-tax information, and confirms that the adviser and software support the case before assuming a standard resident-landlord package is suitable.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What does the agent withhold?Reconcile gross income, expenses and tax deducted using statements and certificates.
What is the actual residence position?Provide the relevant facts; scheme status and statutory tax residence are not identical tests.
Is specialist filing support agreed?Confirm supplementary information, software, treaty or overseas advice scope before purchase.

Two more questions you may have

Does permission to receive gross rent mean no UK tax?

No. It concerns withholding. The annual reporting and liability still need checking.

Can I use only the bank payout for the return?

No. It may already exclude fees and tax credits. Supply the full gross-to-net evidence.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect full agent statements and withholding certificates.
  • Retain any gross-payment approval.
  • Prepare residence and travel information.
  • Gather ownership, costs and foreign-tax evidence.
  • Confirm accepted filing and specialist-advice scope.

title: Foreign Income on a 2025/26 Tax Return: What Changed From April 2025?
excerpt: Foreign income can need reporting in the UK even when it stays in an overseas bank account. Rules changed from 6 April 2025, so advice based only on the old remittance basis may be unsuitable for your 2025/26 return.
metaTitle: Foreign Income 2025/26: Residence and FIG Changes | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Foreign income rules changed in April 2025. Prepare residence history, source-by-country records and foreign tax evidence before considering FIG relief.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer with overseas income sorts country and tax-year records and residence-history timeline with adviser.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax on foreign income: Overview
GOV.UK — Check if you can claim the 4-year foreign income and gains regime

content:
Foreign income can need reporting in the UK even when it stays in an overseas bank account. Rules changed from 6 April 2025, so advice based only on the old remittance basis may be unsuitable for your 2025/26 return.

Residence comes before the calculation

UK residents are generally taxable on foreign income, subject to relevant reliefs and exceptions. Non-residents have a different starting position. Establish your residence status for the year before deciding which income belongs on the return.

Foreign employment, rental income, bank interest, dividends and gains can require different treatment. List each source and the country involved rather than describing the total simply as money from abroad.

The foreign income and gains regime has conditions

From 6 April 2025, the four-year foreign income and gains regime replaced the remittance basis for qualifying new residents. Eligibility generally involves the first four years of UK residence after at least ten consecutive tax years of non-UK residence.

Relief is not automatic just because you moved to the UK recently. Claiming can mean losing the Income Tax Personal Allowance and Capital Gains Tax annual exempt amount, so compare the full outcome before claiming. Historic income arising before April 2025 can raise separate transitional questions.

Tax paid abroad is not automatically ignored or refunded

Foreign tax credit relief and double tax agreements can affect the UK result. Keep the foreign tax calculation and evidence of payment, not just the net amount received. Currency conversion and the relevant reporting period also need support.

For example, an overseas account statement covering a calendar year may need reconciling to the UK tax year. Transferring the balance to the UK later is not necessarily the event that determines when the underlying income is taxable.

Confirm specialist support before purchase

Tell TaxSimba about residence history, foreign income, gains, overseas tax and any earlier remittance-basis claims. Ask whether the case is accepted and what additional work is required. A standard personal return should not be assumed to include a residence analysis, treaty claim or complex transitional calculation without agreement.

Put it into practice

An overseas account does not decide the tax year

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A taxpayer receives foreign interest and keeps it abroad. She identifies when it arose and her residence position for the relevant year rather than assuming tax starts only when funds reach the UK. She provides country-by-country statements, foreign tax paid and residence history. Any four-year FIG eligibility and claim consequences are checked separately, including the effect on allowances. Old pre-April-2025 income and earlier remittance-basis treatment are flagged for specialist transitional review.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
What is the residence history?Establish the year's residence and relevant prior years before choosing a relief.
What income or gain arose in each country?Separate sources, dates, currency and foreign tax evidence.
What would a FIG claim change?Check eligibility, allowances and the complete outcome rather than assuming relief is always beneficial.

Two more questions you may have

Is foreign income automatically outside UK tax if left abroad?

No. Residence, source, timing and available reliefs matter. Keeping money overseas is not a universal exemption.

Does a standard return fee include residence and treaty analysis?

Do not assume so. Confirm specialist scope and pricing before commissioning complex work.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Prepare UK and overseas residence history.
  • List each foreign source and country.
  • Collect gross income, dates and tax-paid evidence.
  • Identify earlier remittance-basis or transitional issues.
  • Agree FIG, treaty and specialist calculation scope.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Sold Shares Outside an ISA? The Records Needed for Capital Gains Tax
excerpt: Selling investments outside an ISA can create a capital gain or loss. The taxable gain is not necessarily the amount withdrawn from the investment account or the profit shown by an app.
metaTitle: Sold Shares Outside an ISA? Capital Gains Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare share-disposal records across brokers, including purchases, fees, corporate actions and later acquisitions needed for UK matching calculations.
featuredImageAlt: An investor organises share acquisition history, disposal statements and broker fees beside an accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax when you sell shares: What you pay it on
GOV.UK — HS284 Shares and Capital Gains Tax (2026)
GOV.UK — Capital Gains Tax rates and allowances

content:
Selling investments outside an ISA can create a capital gain or loss. The taxable gain is not necessarily the amount withdrawn from the investment account or the profit shown by an app.

Identify the account and the disposal

Shares held in an ISA generally have different treatment from taxable holdings. Obtain trade confirmations showing dates, quantities, proceeds and charges, together with the account type. A disposal can also arise from certain gifts or transactions other than an ordinary sale.

Transfers between your own investment accounts should be explained so the accountant does not treat every movement as a sale. Corporate actions and employee share arrangements can require additional records.

Purchase history matters

UK share-matching rules can involve acquisitions on the same day, purchases within the following 30 days and a pooled holding. Selling through one broker does not necessarily mean only that broker's purchases are relevant.

For example, if you sell shares in one account and buy the same shares shortly afterwards in another taxable account, the transactions may interact. A platform's isolated profit figure may not reflect the correct UK matching calculation.

Consider the whole year's gains and losses

The annual exempt amount for an individual is £3,000 for 2025/26, subject to the applicable rules. Reporting can still be required in some circumstances even where there is no tax to pay. Other disposals and allowable losses need considering together.

Do not apply a single capital gains rate without checking the year, asset type and your wider taxable income. A dividend payment is income and should not be confused with a gain on disposing of the shares.

Prepare a complete file

Supply all relevant broker reports, historic acquisition costs, previous pooling calculations, corporate-action documents and loss records. Explain any missing history before the return is prepared.

TaxSimba can confirm whether the investment calculations fit the selected service. Complex share schemes, substantial transaction histories or foreign reporting may need additional work, which should be agreed before relying on a standard tax-return price.

Put it into practice

A second broker can affect the first sale's calculation

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A taxpayer sells shares through one taxable brokerage account and buys the same class shortly afterwards through another. He supplies both histories, acquisition costs and earlier pool workings rather than relying on the first platform's profit display. The accountant checks the UK matching rules, including relevant same-day and following-30-day acquisitions. ISA holdings, dividends and other disposals are identified separately. Withdrawn cash is not itself the gain, and a low current account balance does not settle reporting.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Which account and asset were disposed of?Keep confirmations showing account type, dates, quantities, proceeds and charges.
Are matching acquisitions elsewhere included?Provide all relevant broker histories and prior pool calculations.
What other gains or losses occurred?Review the complete tax year and reporting conditions rather than one transaction alone.

Two more questions you may have

Can I use the app's displayed gain without checking?

Not safely where history, other brokers or UK matching rules are missing. Provide the underlying transactions.

Are dividends included in the capital gain?

They are a separate income item. Keep dividend statements distinct from disposal proceeds and acquisition costs.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Collect all relevant broker trade confirmations.
  • Identify ISA and taxable accounts.
  • Locate acquisition costs and pool workings.
  • Record corporate actions and matching purchases.
  • List other gains, losses and reporting questions.

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.

title: Crypto Reporting From 2026: What Providers Tell HMRC and What You Still Do
excerpt: New crypto reporting arrangements mean providers can collect and report information about users and transactions. That reporting does not replace your responsibility to work out whether you have taxable income or gains.
metaTitle: Crypto Reporting From 2026: What You Still Need to Do | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Provider crypto reporting does not file your tax return. Reconcile calendar-year reports with UK tax years and keep complete wallet and exchange histories.
featuredImageAlt: A crypto user receives a platform information report while maintaining their own complete transaction ledger.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Information you need to give to UK cryptoasset service providers
GOV.UK — Check if you need to report cryptoasset data to HMRC
GOV.UK — Check if you need to pay tax when you sell cryptoassets

content:
New crypto reporting arrangements mean providers can collect and report information about users and transactions. That reporting does not replace your responsibility to work out whether you have taxable income or gains.

What changed for providers?

Under the Cryptoasset Reporting Framework, relevant UK service providers began collecting required information from 1 January 2026. The first reporting window is 1 January to 31 May 2027 for the 2026 calendar year.

A provider may ask for identifying details and tax residence information. Check that a request is genuine using the provider's usual secure channels before supplying sensitive information.

Provider reports and personal returns are different

The reporting obligation discussed here belongs to reporting service providers. An ordinary investor does not become responsible for a provider's CARF report merely by holding crypto.

Your own tax position still needs a separate calculation. Provider data may use a calendar year, while your UK return uses the tax year. It may also omit transactions made through other exchanges, wallets or arrangements.

Do not wait for a report to calculate tax

Selling, exchanging one token for another or certain other disposals can create gains or losses. Receiving crypto through work or some reward arrangements can raise Income Tax questions. Withdrawing pounds to a bank is not the only event that matters.

For example, exchanging tokens in February 2026 falls in the 2025/26 UK tax year. The provider's later report does not move that transaction into a different return or postpone the filing obligation.

Reconcile your full transaction history

Keep exchange exports, wallet transfers, transaction identifiers, fees and acquisition records. Identify transfers between wallets you own so they are not automatically counted as disposals, while still checking fees and any other tax consequences.

Ask TaxSimba to confirm whether your crypto work is accepted and priced within the proposed service. A complex history, staking or decentralised finance can need specialist calculations. Accurate records across all providers are more useful than assuming a single exchange's tax summary has completed the whole task.

Put it into practice

The provider's reporting year is not your return year

Illustrative scenario — not a customer case or personal tax calculation.

A token swap in February 2026 falls within the individual's 2025/26 UK tax year. A provider later reporting calendar-year 2026 information does not move that swap into a later personal return or calculate the correct tax automatically. The taxpayer retains exchange exports, wallet transfers, fees and acquisition records across all platforms. He uses the provider's secure channel for genuine tax-residence requests and checks the personal tax position independently of the provider's CARF reporting duties.

A decision guide for this situation

What to check and how to act
CheckPractical action
Provider report or personal tax obligation?Keep the service provider's information-reporting role separate from your own return.
Do report dates align with the UK tax year?Reconcile calendar-year data to 6 April–5 April records.
Is the transaction history complete across platforms?Include wallets, earlier acquisitions and income events, not one exchange's balance alone.

Two more questions you may have

Do I file a provider CARF report simply because I hold crypto?

No. The provider's reporting duty is different from an ordinary investor's personal tax reporting.

Can I wait for a provider report before dealing with an earlier return?

Do not assume it postpones personal filing or payment. Prepare the relevant tax-year calculation from your own complete records.

Your preparation worksheet

Use these prompts to prepare for a conversation with your accountant. No signup is needed to download the plain-text checklist.

  • Export complete exchange and wallet histories.
  • Reconcile calendar-year and tax-year dates.
  • Link transfers between your own wallets.
  • Identify disposals, fees and income events.
  • Verify sensitive-data requests through secure provider channels.
Download the preparation checklist (.txt)

Save completed notes securely. Keep passwords and security codes out of your notes.
